long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Bourgoin-Jallieu, Foriel-Destezet became known publicly through sustained support for classical music rather than an operating role at Adecco. The underlying family fortune came from Philippe Foriel-Destezet, who founded Ecco and combined it with Adia to form Adecco. After his death in 2021, she inherited the principal family wealth, although the private estate allocation remains undisclosed.

Her own public work is philanthropic and increasingly institutional. She has backed the Paris Opera, Philharmonie de Paris, Opéra-Comique, the Aix-en-Provence Festival and other European organisations. At Versailles she helped establish the Royal Opera foundation and serves as vice-president. In Évian, a decade of support culminated in La Source Vive, a chamber-music hall that she financed and founded.
